newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi, Kohl to meet soon to discuss EMU-report.
newsitem.headline: Prodi, Kohl to meet soon to discuss EMU-report.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi is to meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in a bid to overcome German reluctance to see Italy join a European currency union with a first wave of members in 1999, a newspaper reported on Friday.

Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said the meeting was also intended to resolve tensions between the two countries which have been fuelled by recent remarks by Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
The newspaper gave no date for the planned meeting but Milan daily Corriere della Sera said the two leaders could hold talks as early as next week.
A spokesman at the prime minister's office declined any immediate comment.

Dini's comments have led to speculation that Italy could veto either an intergovernmental conference on reforming European Union institutions or enlargement of the EU unless it is admitted to European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Kohl had expressed irritation over Dini's comments at a summit meeting of EU leaders in the Netherlands last week.

The row between the German government and the Bundesbank over a plan by Finance Minister Theo Waigel to revalue gold reserves and transfer part of the gains to Bonn is seen as strengthening Italy's own case for being allowed into EMU.
Italy, which has been accused of resorting to creative accounting to help wrestle down a public sector deficit, could now level the same charge at Germany, analysts say.
The Bundesbank has said the gold revaluation plan could endanger the future stability of a single currency.
